title: Cut PR wait time: 32 of the last 50 PR pytest-run runs were CANCELLED (superseded by a new push before finishing) and 3 of 15 guards runs failed on guard rules a local run would have caught. Make lanes (and the manager) run scripts/ci/run_guards.py + the affected tests locally before every push, never push to a PR while its CI runs unless fixing red, batch register commits, and profile the guards job (13 min median exec, the real floor)
note: Operator 2026-10-29 ~09:55Z verbatim: "We also seem to be spending an inordinate amount of time waiting for CI checks and for merges ... I thought we had a plan to try and cut that down by like making sure we're only checking what's like what's actually changed and not doing the whole suite for every PR. So I want to check if that was actually implemented." MEASURED 09:55Z (GitHub Actions API, last PR runs): CI-DIET + GH-CAPACITY-PR-CI-FANOUT ARE implemented (scripts/ci/pytest_run_scope.py: data mode + affected-tests mode on PRs; landing/merge-slot files excluded). pytest-run PR job: queue median 2.4 / p90 7.1 min, exec median 9.6 / p90 22.8 min (n 25 jobs). guards: queue 2.6 / 6.7, exec 12.8 / 16.2 (n 15). pytest-collect exec 2.5; repo-inventory 0.8. Conclusions over the last 50 PR pytest-run runs: 32 cancelled, 16 success, 2 failure. The loss is churn (re-pushes cancel and restart) and late guard failures, not suite scope. Manager's own register branch (#21147) is a large contributor: ~25 pushes today, each restarting its CI and conflicting with lane row edits. Also an Actions-wide queue (90 runs at 08:17Z) delays system-actions (GH-CAPACITY-INFRA-RUNNER, rank 2).
